Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

effectsurf (development version)

  • The package now lives at https://github.com/max578/effectsurf, with its site at https://max578.github.io/effectsurf/. The README gains a logo, lifecycle, coverage and r-universe badges, and a Related packages section; coverage and lint run on every push.

  • surf_grid() builds a surface from a precomputed grid: a cross-validated loss over two tuning axes, computed outside a model. It refuses a ragged grid naming the missing cells, records a direction that surf_optimum() reads when type is not given, and carries the new "score" type, which print output and captions report as a cross-validated score.

  • The profile PDFs written beside an exported surface no longer exchange x and y: save_profile_pdfs() read the x profile from the matrix rows (one per y) and the y profile from the columns, which errored on a non-square grid and silently swapped the axes on a square one.

  • The same estimand-discard defect is closed at its second locus. surf_slopes(method = "emmeans") dropped slope exactly as surf_comparison() dropped comparison: emmeans::emtrends() computes the derivative dy/dx only, so a request for "eyex", "eydx" or "dyex" silently returned dy/dx while meta$slope recorded the elasticity the object never computed. It now refuses with a typed effectsurf_refusal, naming the backend that does honour the request. Fixing surf_comparison() alone would have left this alive, which is why the class was not declared closed at the time.

  • S7 is declared in Suggests. surf_from_manifest() uses S7:: behind a requireNamespace() guard, but the dependency was never declared, so R CMD check --as-cran reported an undeclared import – a warning introduced by the manifest-ingress commit and not caught there.

Three correctness fixes

  • surf_derivatives() no longer writes fabricated values into estimate. When a derivative surface was effectively constant, the computed values were overwritten with a synthetic linear ramp (0.1% of the value) so plotly’s WebGL renderer would not cull a zero-thickness mesh. The ramp reached surf_data(), surf_tidy(), as.data.frame(), surf_export() and surf_optimum() as if it were a derivative, and surf_optimum() duly reported an optimum at a corner of it. It also widened the range past the threshold of the constancy notice, so the user was never told. The rendering problem is already handled where it belongs – build_scene() sets an explicit zaxis$range for a flat surface – so the residual noise is now collapsed to the constant it represents and the data stays honest.

  • surf_comparison(method = "emmeans") no longer reports an estimand it did not compute. The emmeans backend was called without the comparison argument and always took the pairwise difference of estimated marginal means. A user who asked for comparison = "ratio" or "lnratio" received differences, and es_meta() reported the ratio they had asked for, so nothing in the object or in a plot drawn from it revealed the substitution; a contrast given as a level name or a step size was dropped the same way. Since a ratio is not a difference, and emmeans reaches one only by re-expressing the contrast on a transformed scale – which would give a ratio on a log link and another difference on an identity link – the backend now refuses these combinations with a typed effectsurf_refusal() that names method = "marginaleffects" as the route that honours them. Both fields of meta now record what was computed: "difference", and "pairwise" where that default was applied. The marginaleffects backend is unchanged, and the first tests of the treatment-effect verbs grade every documented comparison against an analytic oracle.

  • surf_prediction(method = "manual") works without a predict_fun. It is a documented method but was not one of ems_predict()’s choices, so it always errored. Every method = "manual" call in the suite happened to pass a predict_fun, which routes to "predict" and hid the path; it is now mapped to the backend it has always meant, and a test calls it with no predict_fun.

Manifest ingress

  • surf_from_manifest() places effectsurf downstream of the orchestra contract. Any member emitting an orchestra_manifest on a surfaceable inferential target – predictions, treatment_effects, breeding_values – can now be rendered without being refitted first. Previously the package consumed fitted model objects only and the string “manifest” did not occur anywhere in it, so it could not sit on a chain behind any member.

  • The manifest is read duck-typed, by property name, so effectsurf imports neither orchestraManifest nor any other member. It consumes the contract and emits nothing back into it, which keeps it a terminal leaf and makes a dependency cycle impossible.

  • effectsurf_refusal() gives the package its first typed abstention, classed orchestra_refusal so the rest of the fleet can route on it. surf_from_manifest() raises a typed refusal in six cases: the object does not present as a manifest, its inferential target has no two-predictor response, the producer already abstained, outputs is empty, the response column cannot be identified, or the grid columns are missing or do not form a complete rectangle. A ragged grid previously became a surface with holes filled by whatever was adjacent.

effectsurf 0.2.0.9000

  • New feature: Post-prediction surface smoothing (smooth parameter). All surf_*() functions now accept a smooth argument that applies mgcv::gam() tensor product smoothing (te(x, y)) to predicted values. This is particularly useful for non-smooth models (random forests, boosted trees, MARS) where raw predictions form jagged or step-function surfaces.
    • smooth = NULL (default): No smoothing – raw predictions displayed.
    • smooth = TRUE: Auto-smooth with te(x, y, k = -1, bs = "tp"), using mgcv’s automatic basis dimension selection (same default as mgcv::s()).
    • smooth = list(k = 15, bs = "cr", smooth_ci = FALSE): Full manual control over basis dimension, basis type, and CI smoothing.
    • Separate smooth fitted per stratum when by is used, preserving interaction structure across groups.
    • Smoothing metadata stored in the effectsurf object for traceability.
  • Previous version (0.1.0.9000) archived to zz_archive/.

effectsurf 0.1.0.9000

  • Initial development version.
  • Core surface functions: surf_prediction(), surf_comparison(), surf_slopes(), surf_cate().
  • Interactive 3D Plotly rendering with categorical stratification.
  • Confidence envelope surfaces.
  • 2D profile projections via surf_profile().
  • Sensitivity analysis via surf_sensitivity().
  • Model-agnostic via marginaleffects (100+ model classes).
  • Optional gratia integration for GAM smooth surfaces.
  • Bundled barley_trials example dataset.
  • HTML export via surf_export().
